transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because things have felt kind of out of control lately. I’d barely settled into my new apartment, and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and redesigning my whole portfolio like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint. It just felt like too much, too fast.
Have you been feeling excessively anxious or worried about things lately?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive worry. I mean, I’ve felt stressed and kind of keyed up, but I haven’t really noticed myself worrying nonstop about specific things.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt abnormally happy or irritable?

Yes. Earlier this month I had moments where I felt almost electric, really upbeat, like everything was suddenly possible. But then it would flip, and I’d snap at people over really small stuff—like a contractor being delayed, or my sister not responding fast enough. It felt way more intense than my usual mood.
Did you have any periods where you didn't need much sleep, yet you still had a lot of energy?
Yes. For several nights, I only slept maybe three or four hours, but I’d wake up feeling like I was completely fine. Like I should just use the extra time to get ahead instead of being tired.
Have you recently engaged in any impulsive or reckless behaviors that might be out of character for you?

Yes. I spent money in a way that really isn’t like me. I bought these expensive light fixtures, some design software add-ons, and even a last-minute flight for a trip I couldn’t really afford. At the time it felt fine, like I’d figure it out, but afterward I realized it had really hit my savings.
How long did these periods of feeling almost electric and really upbeat usually last?
It’s been going on since I moved into this apartment, so… about a month now. The really intense ups and downs have kind of been part of that whole period.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that seemed real but weren't based in reality?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that weren’t there. I’ve had some intense thoughts, but they still felt like my own thoughts, not like something unreal.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were not your own or that someone or something was controlling your mind?
No, I haven’t felt like someone else was controlling my mind. My thoughts can feel fast or intense sometimes, but they still feel like mine.
Have you experienced any periods of feeling persistently sad or empty during the past month?

Yes. Lately I’ve been waking up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest. Even when it’s quiet and nothing is really wrong, I’ll feel like I could just cry over something small, like a coffee mug left in the sink.
How often have you been feeling this heavy, gray feeling in your chest during the past month?

Most mornings, honestly. Not every single minute of the day, but it’s been there a lot this past month—especially when I wake up and the apartment is quiet. It just hits me, that heavy gray feeling, and small things can make me feel like I’m about to cry.
Have you ever felt like you're detached from yourself or the world around you?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can feel kind of numb or checked out sometimes, but I haven’t really felt like I’m outside myself or that the world isn’t real.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being broadcasted so that others could hear them?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve worried what people might think of me, but I haven’t felt like they could actually hear my thoughts.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being controlled by an outside force?
No, I haven’t felt like that. My thoughts feel like my own, even when they’re stressful or hard to shut off.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide during this past month?

Yes… I have had thoughts like that this past month. Not like I’m planning to do anything, but I’ll have these scary thoughts like maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And honestly, the fact that I’m even thinking that really scares me.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt like your thoughts or actions were not your own during these episodes of feeling electric or really upbeat?

No, I don’t think so. Even when I feel really upbeat or kind of charged up, it still feels like it’s me thinking and doing things. Maybe more impulsive or intense, but not like someone else is controlling me.
Have you had any periods during the past month where you felt so low that you couldn't enjoy activities you usually like?

Yes. I’ve had times this past month where I just don’t feel interested in things I usually like. I used to look forward to hiking at Crowders, cooking something nice, or sketching interface ideas just for fun, but lately I’ll just look at my gear or my tablet and feel… nothing really pulling me toward it.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts or actions were being controlled or influenced by something outside of yourself during these episodes?

No… not really. I haven’t noticed anything like an outside force controlling me or influencing what I do. It feels like my own thoughts and choices, even if they’re stronger or harder to slow down sometimes.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts or actions were not under your control during these episodes of feeling electric or really upbeat?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can get carried away or act faster than I normally would, but it still feels like I’m the one making the choices. Not like I’m completely out of control.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts or actions were not your own during these episodes of feeling really low?
No, I don’t think so. When I’m really low, the thoughts still feel like mine… just heavier and harder to get away from. I haven’t felt like they belonged to someone else or anything like that.
Have you had any periods during the past month where you felt so low that you couldn't get out of bed?

Yeah… there have been mornings like that this past month. I wake up and there’s this heavy, gray feeling in my chest, and it feels really hard to get myself up. Even if the apartment is quiet and nothing’s actually wrong, I can feel like I might cry over something small, like a mug left in the sink.
